question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y & =5{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}∼N(5{\mu }_{1}+{\mu }_{2},{5}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(5\cdot 1+4,25\cdot 0.4+6) \\  & ∼N(9,16).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =9$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{16}=4.$ 

We want to find $P(Y<13.4).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<13.4) & =P(Z<\frac{13.4-9}{4}) \\  & =P(Z<1.1) \\  & =Φ(1.1)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.1)≈0.8643.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(Y<13.4)≈0.86.
$$
